title: Flat terms of the explicit finite-projective ring dual
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, with A-modules realized on the bottom-topology one-object ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Let P be a cochain complex such that every evaluated term P^n is finite projective over A. Define D=Hom_A^\bullet(P,A[0]) using the shared Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], with the ring sheaf in degree zero. Then D^n is a flat sheaf of modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] for every integer n. No boundedness is required.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), finite-projective dual argument; projectivity of the dual also Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Lemmas.lean, Module.dual_projective (lines 145-147)

proof.text: Use the specified product fan of the shared Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] and its projections [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Lift the family whose component at p=-n is the identity and whose other components are zero. The lift followed by that projection is the identity by the product factorization equation. For the reverse composite, apply product extensionality: at p=-n the factorization equation gives identity, and every other target is zero since the single complex is zero in degree p+n. The single-complex term isomorphism identifies the surviving target with the unit ring sheaf. This constructs the isomorphism D^n ≅ internalHom(P^(-n),A).

Evaluate internal Hom at the sole object. Evaluation of a slice morphism at the identity slice object is a linear map P^(-n)(*) → A. It is injective since the slice has only one object; it is surjective by extending a linear map to the one-object presheaves and restricting it to the slice. This is a linear equivalence. Install the given finite and projective instances, then apply Mathlib Module.dual_projective, Module.Flat.of_projective and Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv to obtain flatness of the evaluated internal Hom module.

Every site object equals the chosen point, so flatness holds at every evaluation of the internal Hom presheaf. By Mathlib Module.Flat tensorRight preserves finite limits in each module category. PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits then shows tensorRight for this presheaf preserves finite limits. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] with the identity ring map. Mathlib gives an isomorphism from its sheafification to the original sheaf via the sheafification-adjunction counit. Transport exactFunctor across the tensorRight natural isomorphism induced by that counit, and then across the dual-term isomorphism. This is precisely flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. No boundedness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is used.

lean.statement: theorem perfectRingDual_term_isFlat {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (P : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (hp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective A ((P.X n).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) (hf : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite A ((P.X n).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) : ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((perfectRingDual P).X n)
